summary_grc: ξένος τις εἰς τὸ ἐργαστήριον εἰσέρχεται· «πόθεν ἥκεις; ποῖ βαίνεις;»
summary_en: This, that and that over there (οὗτος, ὅδε, ἐκεῖνος); asking where from and where to; and how Greek says when, how long and within what time.
caption_grc: «πόθεν ἥκεις, ὦ ξένε;» — «ἐκ Μιλήτου· αὕτη μὲν ἡ κύλιξ καλή ἐστιν, ἐκείνη δὲ καλλίων.»

glosses.value: across, on the far side of (+ genitive)

sentences.text: «πότε ἦλθες;» «χθὲς ἦλθον· δέκα γὰρ ἡμέρας ἔπλει τὸ πλοῖον. τοῦ δὲ χειμῶνος οὐδεὶς πλεῖ· νῦν δὲ ἔαρ ἐστίν.»
ὁ ἔμπορος τὰς κύλικας σκοπεῖ· «αὕτη μὲν ἡ κύλιξ καλή ἐστιν, ἐκείνη δὲ καλλίων· ἥδε δὲ ἡ ὑδρία καλλίστη πασῶν.»

glosses.value: ὅδε | ἥδε: this one here (in my hand)

sentences.text: «πόσας κύλικας βούλει, ὦ Θεόδωρε;» ἐρωτᾷ ὁ Ἀρίστων.
«τριάκοντα τούτων τῶν κυλίκων· ἐν Μιλήτῳ γὰρ αἱ Ἀθηναῖαι κύλικες τιμὴν μεγάλην ἔχουσιν.»
ὁ Ἀρίστων· «τοσαύτας κύλικας οὐκ ἔχω νῦν· δεῖ με τρεῖς ἡμέρας πονεῖν.»

glosses.value: it is necessary: δεῖ με πονεῖν 'I must work'

sentences.text: «καλῶς· τέτταρας ἡμέρας ἐν ταῖς Ἀθήναις μένω, τῇ δὲ πέμπτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀποπλέω.»
ἡ Ἐλπὶς ἐν τῇ θύρᾳ ἵσταται· «ποῖ δὲ πλεῖς, ὦ ξένε;» «πάλιν εἰς τὴν Μίλητον.»
ἡ Ἐλπὶς ἐρωτᾷ· «ἆρα ἐφοβοῦ ποτε ἐν τῇ θαλάττῃ; μεγάλη γάρ πού ἐστιν.»

glosses.value: ever, at some time (indefinite: no accent of its own)
I suppose, somewhere (indefinite που; ποῦ; asks 'where?')

sentences.text: ὁ δὲ Θεόδωρος γελᾷ· «ἐφοβούμην ποτέ, ὅτε εἴκοσιν ἐτῶν ἦν καὶ χειμὼν ἦν· νῦν δὲ οὐδέποτε. οἱ γὰρ ναῦται ἀεί που σῴζουσι τὸ πλοῖον.»
«μένε παρ' ἡμῖν τήνδε τὴν νύκτα, ὦ Θεόδωρε», λέγει ὁ Ἀρίστων· ὁ οὖν ξένος ἐκείνην τὴν νύκτα ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένει.

glosses.value: παρ' ἡμῖν: with us, at our house

grammar.md:
**Three words for 'this' and 'that'.** Greek points with three demonstratives, depending on distance from the speaker:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε** | *this (here, by me)* | the article + -δε: τόνδε, τῆσδε, τῷδε … |
| **οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο** | *this, that (by you; what was just said)* | see the paradigm: τούτου, ταύτης, τοῦτον, ταῦτα … |
| **ἐκεῖνος, ἐκείνη, ἐκεῖνο** | *that (over there; far away)* | declined like αὐτός, neuter -ο |

οὗτος looks irregular but follows one rule: the stem has **-ου-** wherever the ending has ο or ω (τούτου, τούτῳ, τοῦτον, τούτων) and **-αυ-** wherever it has α or η (αὕτη, ταύτης, ταῦτα). The neuter singular has no -ν: τοῦτο, τόδε, ἐκεῖνο.

With a noun, a demonstrative always takes the article and stands **outside** the article + noun: *αὕτη ἡ κύλιξ* or *ἡ κύλιξ αὕτη* 'this cup', never *ἡ αὕτη κύλιξ*. Alone, οὗτος often means 'he, she': *οὗτος δὲ λέγει* 'and he says'. ὅδε also points forward to what is about to be said (*τάδε λέγει* 'he says this: …'), οὗτος back to what was just said.

**Asking and not asking: interrogative vs indefinite adverbs.** The question words have an accent and open the sentence; the same words without their own accent (enclitics) mean *some-*:

| question | indefinite |
|---|---|
| **ποῦ;** *where?* | **που** *somewhere; I suppose* |
| **πόθεν;** *from where?* | ποθέν *from somewhere* |
| **ποῖ;** *to where?* | ποι *to somewhere* |
| **πότε;** *when?* | **ποτε** *at some time, once, ever* |
| **πῶς;** *how?* | πως *somehow* |
| **τίς; τί;** *who? what?* | τις, τι *someone, something* |

The indefinites lean on the word before them: *ἐγώ ποτε εἶδον* 'I once saw', *ἆρα ἐφοβοῦ ποτε;* 'were you ever afraid?', *μεγάλη πού ἐστιν* 'it is big, I suppose'.

**Expressions of time.** Three cases, three questions:

| case | question | example |
|---|---|---|
| dative | *when?* (a point) | **τῇ πέμπτῃ ἡμέρᾳ** 'on the fifth day', **τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ** 'the next day', ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτί |
| accusative | *how long?* (a stretch) | **δέκα ἡμέρας** 'for ten days', **τρεῖς ἡμέρας πονεῖν** |
| genitive | *within what time?* | **τοῦ χειμῶνος** 'in winter', **νυκτός** 'by night', **ἑσπέρας** 'in the evening' |

Age uses the genitive too: *εἴκοσιν ἐτῶν* 'twenty years old'. Ordinals (πρῶτος, δεύτερος, τρίτος, τέταρτος, πέμπτος …) are adjectives declined like καλός.

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Α · Fill in the endings of the demonstratives.
exercises.template: αὕτ___ ἡ κύλιξ καλή ἐστιν. ἐκείν___ ἡ ὑδρία καλλίων ἐστίν. τούτ___ τῶν κυλίκων τριάκοντα βούλομαι. τήν___ τὴν νύκτα ὁ ξένος μένει.
exercises.explain: αὕτη and ἐκείνη agree with feminine nouns; τούτων is genitive plural; τήνδε = τήν + δε.

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Β · ___ ἥκεις, ὦ ξένε; — ἐκ Μιλήτου.
exercises.explain: The answer is 'from Miletus', so the question is 'from where?': πόθεν.

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Β · ___ πλεῖς; — εἰς τὴν Μίλητον.
exercises.explain: 'To Miletus' answers ποῖ; 'to where?'.

exercises.prompt: Μελέτημα Β · τοῦ ___ οὐδεὶς πλεῖ.
exercises.explain: Time within which: genitive, τοῦ χειμῶνος 'in (the course of) winter'.

exercises.prompt: ἔμπορος
exercises.explain: ὁ ἔμπορος: the merchant who travels by ship to trade.

exercises.prompt: πλοῖον
exercises.explain: τὸ πλοῖον: a merchant ship.

exercises.explain: ταύτην τὴν νύκτα: -αυ- before the α/η endings.

exercises.prompt: Give the masculine genitive plural of ἐκεῖνος ('of those men').
exercises.explain: ἐκείνων, like αὐτῶν.

exercises.prompt: Give the neuter nominative plural of ὅδε ('these things, the following').
exercises.explain: τάδε = τά + δε: 'the following'.

exercises.prompt: Give the genitive singular of χειμών (as in 'in winter').
exercises.explain: τοῦ χειμῶνος: stem χειμων-, genitive -ος.

exercises.prompt: Parse ταύτῃ.
exercises.explain: ταύτῃ: dative singular feminine of οὗτος, e.g. ταύτῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ 'on this day'.

exercises.prompt: Parse τῶνδε.
exercises.explain: τῶν + δε: genitive plural of ὅδε, 'of these'.

exercises.prompt: ὁ ξένος ___ τὴν νύκτα ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ μένει.
exercises.explain: ταύτην τὴν νύκτα: accusative, agreeing with τὴν νύκτα (how long he stays).

exercises.prompt: ὁ Θεόδωρος ___ ἡμέρας ἐν ταῖς Ἀθήναις μένει.
exercises.explain: 'For four days' is a stretch of time: accusative, τέτταρας ἡμέρας.

exercises.prompt: τῇ ___ ἡμέρᾳ ἀποπλεῖ.
exercises.explain: 'On the fifth day': dative of time when, with the ordinal agreeing with ἡμέρᾳ.

exercises.prompt: ἆρα εἶδές ___ τὴν Μίλητον; (ever)
exercises.explain: 'Ever' is the indefinite ποτε, without its own accent; πότε; would ask 'when?'.

exercises.prompt: Make it plural: οὗτος ὁ ἔμπορος ἐκ Μιλήτου ἥκει. → … οἱ ἔμποροι ἐκ Μιλήτου ἥκουσιν.
exercises.explain: οὗτοι οἱ ἔμποροι: masculine nominative plural.

exercises.prompt: Turn the point in time into a length of time: τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ πονεῖ (on the third day). → … πονεῖ (for three days).
exercises.explain: Duration goes in the accusative: τρεῖς ἡμέρας.

culture.title: Miletus, Ionia and the sea road to Athens
culture.md:
Miletus lay on the coast of **Ionia**, the Greek-speaking strip of western Asia Minor, where the river Maeander met the sea. In the sixth century it had been the richest Greek city of the east: home of the first philosophers (Thales, Anaximander, Anaximenes), mother of dozens of colonies around the Black Sea, famous for its fine wool and purple-dyed cloth. The Persians destroyed it in 494 BC at the end of the Ionian Revolt, and the new city was rebuilt on a strict grid of straight streets, an idea later associated with the Milesian planner Hippodamus, who laid out the Piraeus for Athens. In 432 BC Miletus was an ally of Athens in the Delian League and paid tribute every year; twenty years later it would revolt, but nobody in Ariston's workshop knows that yet.

A merchant like Theodorus sailed only between spring and autumn. Greek merchant ships (πλοῖα) were broad wooden sailing vessels with a single square sail, and winter storms made the Aegean crossing too dangerous; Hesiod already advised farmers to haul their boats ashore when the Pleiades set in November. From Miletus to the Piraeus is roughly 300 km by way of Samos, Icaria and the Cyclades, a week or two depending on the wind, with nights spent at anchor. Ionian traders brought wool, dyed textiles, wine and slaves; from Athens they carried home silver, olive oil and painted pottery, which was prized all over the Aegean. Athenian cups have been dug up from Spain to the Crimea.
